sections.heading: Why Data Analyst Resumes Are Failing ATS Systems in 2026
sections.content:
Data analyst roles are among the most competitive in the 2026 job market. Recruiters at FAANG, tier-1 consultancies, and fast-growing tech companies routinely receive 200–500 applications per data analyst opening. The first filter is almost always an Applicant Tracking System.

AIResume's research team analysed 512 data analyst resume submissions from Q4 2025–Q1 2026. The findings were stark: only 14% of resumes scored above 80/100 on AIResume's ATS engine, and those were exclusively built with role-specific templates or AI assistance.

Key finding: Generic resume builders (Resume-Now, CakeCV free tier) produced DA resumes with an average keyword match score of 34/100. AIResume's DA-specific AI engine produced an average of 76/100 — a 124% improvement.

sections.heading: Tools Stack and Certifications Section
sections.content:
The tools section is the highest-value section for keyword density in a data analyst resume. AIResume's DA template auto-formats this section into four clean categories:

Languages

Python, R, SQL, SAS

Visualisation

Tableau, Power BI, Looker

Databases & Warehousing

pandas, NumPy, scikit-learn, Spark

For certifications, AIResume's research team recommends listing credentials in this priority order, based on recruiter survey data:

  2. Microsoft Power BI Data Analyst — cited by 37%
  3. Tableau Desktop Specialist / Certified Data Analyst — cited by 31%
  4. AWS Certified Data Analytics — cited by 22%
